_what_this_is: Verdicts measured by studio/_tools/cast_proof.py on 2026-08-04 and reached by LOOKING at studio/samples/cast_proof/*.jpg, cell by cell. They belong on the character cards. They are in a separate file because the brief that produced them scoped ownership to cast_proof.py and samples/cast_proof/ and said in as many words not to edit character cards. Whoever owns studio/characters/ should merge each block into its card; nothing here is speculative and every claim names the sheet it came from.
_method_in_one_line: Five places no training set contained (laundromat, snowfield, library_reading_room, subway_platform, market_street), one seed per place shared by every arm, identical prompt text in every arm, only a weight changing. 126 cells.

VIRO.proof_verdict: HOLDS, AND HE IS THE CHARACTER THE LoRA IS WORTH MOST TO. MEASURED by looking at studio/samples/cast_proof/viro_places.jpg and viro_pinned_faces.jpg - five places the training set never contained, one seed per place, the same prompt in every arm, only a weight changing. WITH the LoRA at 0.85 plus the sheet, the same man appears in 5 of 5: pale wheat-blond wavy hair over darker roots, narrow half-lidded amber eyes, thin straight brows, a closed smirk, the gold ear stud, the teal number 7. WITHOUT the LoRA but WITH the sheet at IPAdapter 0.6, a consistent man also appears - but it is a DIFFERENT man, browner-haired, rounder-eyed, younger and softer in 5 of 5. That is the finding that matters for him: the sheet is not a weaker version of the LoRA, it is a second, competing answer to who VIRO is. WITHOUT both, on the danbooru tags alone, there are five different people - dark-haired, large-eyed, several reading as girls or children despite `1boy`, one with visibly different skin. His tags are generic enough that they describe nobody in particular, which is exactly why the trained weights carry him.
VIRO.proof_cost: TWO COSTS, BOTH VISIBLE IN viro_places.jpg. (1) THE SCENE. At 0.85 all five places are bleached toward the training set's cream backdrop - the subway platform loses its tiled walls and tunnel mouth and becomes a pale corridor, the market street loses its crowd and depth. The no-LoRA rows in the same grid keep saturated, detailed rooms. (2) THE FRAMING. All five LoRA cells are tight busts with the head filling the upper frame, because the LoRA was trained on sixteen head-and-shoulders turnaround views and imports the framing along with the face. The tags-only row at the same seeds gives wide establishing shots. If a shot needs him small in a big room, the LoRA will fight it. 0.85 was NOT compared against 0.5 in this run - it was used because studio/loras/character-viro.json recommends it - so `use 0.5 instead` is a reasonable guess and not a measurement. Run studio/_tools/lora_strength_sweep.py VIRO to settle it.
VIRO.proof_disagreement: THE CARD AND THE WEIGHTS DISAGREE ABOUT HIS HAIR. `tags` says 'long dark brown curly hair'. At strength 0.85 he renders pale wheat-blond over darker roots in 5 of 5, and it is the first thing you see. The sheet-only arm renders him brown, i.e. closer to the card. This is the same drift character-viro.json already records as 'pale blond over the crown falling to a dark brown curly ponytail' - but at 0.85 it is no longer a highlight, it is his hair colour. Either the card should say so or the LoRA should be retrained from a corrected sheet.

NIKA.proof_verdict: HOLDS AT 0.5, AND THERE IS A COUNTABLE MARKER. MEASURED from studio/samples/cast_proof/nika_pinned_faces.jpg - five places, one seed each, framing pinned so the five faces are comparable. WHICH EYE IS WHICH COLOUR is the cleanest identity fact this character has, because `tags` names two eye colours and no side, so nothing in the prompt can decide it. Amber on the viewer's left: 5 of 5 with the LoRA, 3 of 5 with the reference sheet alone, 2 of 5 on tags alone - which is chance. The LoRA is the only thing that holds it. The facial scar also appears in 3 of 5 LoRA cells and in neither control reliably. BUT HER LEAD OVER THE CONTROL IS SMALL, and that is the honest half: silver hair, heterochromia, the grey blazer and the red tie all render from the tags alone, so the tags-only arm is a recognisable NIKA with a wandering face rather than a stranger. Her card was right to say the control is not a stranger; this quantifies how far from one.
NIKA.proof_cost: The five scenes are flattened and desaturated even at 0.5 - compare the LoRA row of nika_places.jpg against the tags-only row of the same grid at the same seeds. It is milder than the dark-grey-void collapse her card records at 0.85, which is consistent with the existing note that the damage scales with strength and with distance from the training backdrop. Framing also collapses to a centred bust in 5 of 5.
NIKA.proof_stray: IN THE TAGS-ONLY ARM SHE GREW TEAL AND GREEN HAIR STREAKS that appear on no card - in the laundromat cell (a room full of teal machines) and the subway cell. The place bleeds into the character when nothing is holding her. Neither the LoRA arm nor the sheet arm does it.

PIP.proof_verdict: HOLDS, BUT HIS LoRA IS THE LEAST NECESSARY OF THE THREE. MEASURED from studio/samples/cast_proof/pip_pinned_faces.jpg and pip_places.jpg. Across five unseen places all THREE arms - LoRA plus sheet, sheet only, and bare danbooru tags - return a recognisable ginger freckled boy in a yellow raincoat holding a green toy dinosaur. His tags are specific enough ('orange hair, messy hair, freckles, gap teeth' plus a named garment) that the description already does most of the work. THE ONE THING THE LoRA RELIABLY ADDS IS A DEFECT: the white crown tuft, present in 5 of 5 LoRA cells and 0 of 5 in both controls. The most reliable evidence that his trained weights are active is an artefact his card never asked for. That is not an argument against the LoRA - it does steady his eye size and face proportion - but anyone budgeting twenty minutes of training time per character should spend it on the character whose description is vaguest, not on PIP.
PIP.proof_correction: CORRECTION TO THIS CARD, MEASURED: the note says of the odd boots 'Nothing holds them, LoRA or not.' That is true of the ANIME path only. On the qwen reference-sheet path (studio/samples/cast_proof/pip_qwen.jpg) one red boot and one green boot rendered correctly in 5 of 5 places, from an upper-body sheet that has never contained them, because the prose prompt states them as a sentence and the framing came out full-body. Narrow the claim to the anime tag path.
PIP.proof_cost: Scenes pale at 0.5 rather than collapse - the subway platform cell of pip_places.jpg is the worst, washing to near-white. Consistent with his card's existing note that a light warm training backdrop costs less than a dark one.

_applies_to_every_character.style_and_identity_cannot_be_stacked: MEASURED on three characters x three styles x four rungs (studio/samples/cast_proof/*_style.jpg). With the reference sheet loaded through IPAdapter at its shipping weight of 0.6, EIGHT OF NINE styled cells are visually indistinguishable from the no-style cell beside them: an ink_wash prompt carrying 'monochrome, greyscale, brush stroke' returned a full-colour digital anime picture, cel_anime_90s returned no grain and no palette shift, retro_shoujo_70s returned no shoujo eyes. The ninth (NIKA under ink_wash) greys the ROOM but leaves the character in full colour and produces no brushwork. The hue_vs_unstyled figures in _metrics.json agree: with the sheet on, 16 of 18 cells moved less than 20; with it off, 14 of 18 moved more. Dropping the IPAdapter to 0.0 and leaving the character LoRA ON, all three styles land in all three characters AND the character still holds - VIRO comes back as a saturated 90s cel with his number 7, NIKA as a near-monochrome ink drawing with her heterochromia and star pin, PIP as an ink wash with his white tuft. THE SUPPRESSOR IS THE IPAdapter, NOT THE LoRA. This is the one actionable recipe from the whole run: to put a cast member in a style on the anime engine, use the trained LoRA and set the IPAdapter weight to 0. A character with no LoRA cannot be styled and held at the same time on this engine at all.
_applies_to_every_character.qwen_needs_a_photographic_sheet: MEASURED from *_qwen.jpg. Through Qwen-Image-Edit the reference sheet holds identity across all five places and costs the scene NOTHING - the laundromat, snowfield, library, subway and market all render in full detail, which the anime LoRA path does not manage. But the sheet imports its own medium: with the anime sheet, every cell came back an illustration however loudly the prompt said 'photograph'. VIRO is the only character with sheet_photo_viro.png, and his photographic row is five photographs of one man. NIKA and PIP cannot be photographed until somebody runs studio/_tools/qwen_sheet.py for them.
_applies_to_every_character.a_shipped_negative_fights_this_arm: workflows/14_qwen_edit_ref.json node 11 carries 'photorealistic, 3d render' in its NEGATIVE while every prompt through it asks for a photograph. It was left as shipped so arm D measured the product rather than a patched graph, but it is a defect in a shared workflow and belongs to whoever owns workflows/.
